name: What is required to convert a single-sink vanity to a double-sink vanity?

mainEntity.name: What is required to convert a single-sink vanity to a double-sink vanity?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upgrading from a single vanity to a double sink requires adequate wall width—typically at least 60 inches—to provide usable counter space and comfortable elbow room. Structurally, the plumbing must be split or extended: you will need two sets of water supply lines and either dual drain connections or an approved sanitary tee setup meeting local plumbing codes. If your current bathroom only has a single electrical outlet or centered lighting, you will also need to adjust wiring to accommodate two mirrors and balanced light fixtures.
acceptedAnswer.description: You need at least 60 inches of wall space, split water supply lines, updated drainage to support dual basins, and relocated lighting and electrical outlets.
